advisor.trigger.constraint_disabled.titl: The {kindKey, select, foreign_key {foreign key} unique {unique} primary_key {primary key} exclusion {exclusion} constraint_trigger {constraint trigger} constraint {constraint} other {{kind}}} {name} is not enforced
advisor.trigger.constraint_disabled.deta: The internal triggers that enforce {kindKey, select, foreign_key {foreign key} unique {unique} primary_key {primary key} exclusion {exclusion} constraint_trigger {constraint trigger} constraint {constraint} other {{kind}}} {name} on {table} in database {datname} are disabled ({triggers}), as ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL leaves them. Rows that violate the constraint can be written while they stay disabled.
advisor.trigger.constraint_disabled.reme: Run ALTER TABLE {tableSQL} ENABLE TRIGGER ALL, then look for rows written meanwhile that violate {name}: enabling the triggers does not check existing rows.
advisor.trigger.user_disabled.title: Trigger {trigger} on {table} is disabled
advisor.trigger.user_disabled.detail: Trigger {trigger} ({timing} {events}, {level}, function {function}) on {table} in database {datname} is disabled: writes to the table no longer run it.
advisor.trigger.user_disabled.remediatio: If the trigger should run, ALTER TABLE {tableSQL} ENABLE TRIGGER {triggerSQL}. If it is retired, drop it so its state is not mistaken for an accident.
advisor.index.fk_unindexed.title: Foreign key {constraint} on {table} has no index
advisor.index.fk_unindexed.detail: No index on {table} in database {datname} leads with ({columns}), the columns of foreign key {constraint} referencing {referenced}. Every DELETE of a row of {referenced}, and every UPDATE of its key, scans {table} ({size}) for referencing rows while holding its locks.
advisor.index.fk_unindexed.remediation: If rows of {referenced} are deleted or their keys updated, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON {tableSQL} ({columnsSQL}). If they never are, the index is not needed.
advisor.extension.upgrade_available.deta: Database {datname} runs extension {name} {installed}; the installed packages carry {version}. Until the extension is updated, the database keeps the objects of the older version.
advisor.extension.upgrade_available.reme: Read the extension's release notes, then, connected to {datname} as its owner, ALTER EXTENSION {nameSQL} UPDATE.
advisor.postgis.upgrade_available.title: PostGIS in database {datname} is older than its library
advisor.postgis.upgrade_available.detail: The PostGIS packages were updated but the extensions of database {datname} were not ({versions}). Its SQL functions still come from the older release while the library is the newer one.
advisor.postgis.upgrade_available.remedi: Connected to {datname} as a superuser, SELECT postgis_extensions_upgrade(); after reading the PostGIS upgrade notes.
advisor.postgis.spatial_unindexed.title: Spatial column {table}.{column} has no spatial index
advisor.postgis.spatial_unindexed.detail: No valid GiST, SP-GiST or BRIN index on {table} in database {datname} starts with {type} column {column} (about {rows} rows). Bounding-box searches (&&, ST_Intersects, ST_DWithin) on it read the whole table.
advisor.postgis.spatial_unindexed.remedi: If the column is searched spatially, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON {tableSQL} USING gist ({columnSQL}).
advisor.postgis.srid_unknown.title: Spatial column {table}.{column} has no known coordinate system
advisor.postgis.srid_unknown.detail: Column {column} of {table} in database {datname} ({type}({subtype})) {noSRID, select, true {is declared without an SRID (0)} other {is declared with SRID {srid}, which spatial_ref_sys does not define}}, so PostGIS cannot transform its values or measure them in real units.
advisor.postgis.srid_unknown.remediation: Find the coordinate system the data was captured in and declare it: ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE {type}({subtype}, <srid>) USING ST_SetSRID(column, <srid>), or add the missing definition to spatial_ref_sys.
advisor.postgis.srid_mixed.title: Geometry columns in database {datname} use {count} coordinate systems
advisor.postgis.srid_mixed.detail: The geometry columns of database {datname} are declared in {parts}. A spatial join or comparison between columns of different SRIDs fails, or needs ST_Transform on every row.
advisor.postgis.srid_mixed.remediation: If the columns are compared with each other, store them in one SRID, or keep a transformed, indexed copy of the ones that are joined.
advisor.sequence.exhaustion_risk.title: Sequence {name} has used {used}% of its range
advisor.sequence.exhaustion_risk.detail: Sequence {name} in database {datname} ({dataType}, increment {increment}) is at {lastValue}; {remaining} values remain before {limit}. Once they run out, {linked, select, true {inserts into {column}} other {inserts that draw from it}} fail.
advisor.sequence.exhaustion_risk.remedia: {limitBy, select, column {The type of column {column} sets the limit: {widen}. This rewrites the table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, and the columns that reference it through foreign keys need the same change; on a large table, add a bigint column, fill it in batches and swap it in instead.{bigintFix, select, true { Then ALTER SEQUENCE {seqSQL} AS bigint.} other {}}} type {The sequence's own type sets the limit. ALTER SEQUENCE {seqSQL} AS bigint raises it without rewriting any table.} maxvalue {The sequence's MAXVALUE sets the limit. ALTER SEQUENCE {seqSQL} NO MAXVALUE raises it to the bigint limit without rewriting any table.} other {The sequence's MINVALUE sets the limit. ALTER SEQUENCE {seqSQL} NO MINVALUE lowers it to the bigint limit without rewriting any table.}}
advisor.sequence.column_narrower.title: Column {column} overflows before sequence {name} runs out
advisor.sequence.column_narrower.detail: Sequence {name} in database {datname} is {dataType} (bounds {min} to {max}) but feeds column {column}: inserts fail once it passes {limit}, whatever its own limit says.
advisor.sequence.column_narrower.remedia: {widen} (this rewrites the table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock), or, if the column is meant to stay as it is, give the sequence the column's bound (ALTER SEQUENCE {seqSQL} AS {columnType}) so the limit is stated where it applies.
advisor.sequence.value_hidden.title: pglens cannot read the values of {count, plural, one {# sequence} other {# sequences}} in database {datname}
advisor.sequence.value_hidden.detail: The monitoring role has neither SELECT nor USAGE on {count, plural, one {# sequence} other {# sequences}} of database {datname} ({examples}), so how close they are to their limit is unknown; only a column narrower than its sequence is still detected.
advisor.sequence.value_hidden.remediatio: Run the agent at tier 1 (pg_read_all_data), or GRANT SELECT ON SEQUENCE ... TO the monitoring role for the sequences to watch. Never grant USAGE: it allows nextval(), which advances the sequence.
advisor.partition.default_has_rows.title: Default partition {defaultPartition} holds about {rows} rows
advisor.partition.default_has_rows.detai: Rows of {table} in database {datname} that match no partition land in its default partition {defaultPartition} (about {rows} rows). Creating a partition for a range that has rows there fails until they are moved, and attaching any partition scans the default partition.
advisor.partition.default_has_rows.remed: Create the partitions those rows belong to: in one transaction, ALTER TABLE {tableSQL} DETACH PARTITION {defaultSQL}, create the missing partitions, move the rows with INSERT INTO {tableSQL} SELECT ... and DELETE, then ATTACH PARTITION {defaultSQL} DEFAULT.
advisor.partition.future_missing.title: {lapsed, select, true {Partitions of {table} ended {durationUnit, select, day {{durationCount, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}} other {{durationCount, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}}} ago} other {Partitions of {table} end in {durationUnit, select, day {{durationCount, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}} other {{durationCount, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}}}}}
advisor.partition.future_missing.detail: {table} in database {datname} is partitioned by range ({partitionKey}), and its partitions reach {until}: {consequence, select, fail_future {rows past that point will fail to insert} default_future {rows past that point will land in the default partition {defaultPartition}} default_past {rows since then land in the default partition {defaultPartition}} other {inserts of rows since then fail}}.
advisor.partition.future_missing.remedia: Create the next partitions ahead of time (CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF {tableSQL} FOR VALUES FROM (...) TO (...)), and schedule their creation, with pg_partman or a cron job, so the table never runs out.
advisor.partition.index_invalid.title: {count, plural, one {# partitioned index of {table} is not valid} other {# partitioned indexes of {table} are not valid}}
advisor.partition.index_invalid.detail: {count, plural, one {Partitioned index {indexes} of {table} in database {datname} is not valid} other {Partitioned indexes {indexes} of {table} in database {datname} are not valid}}: some partitions have no matching index attached, so queries on them cannot use it.{unique, select, true { A unique index among them does not enforce uniqueness on the partitions that lack it.} other {}}
advisor.partition.index_invalid.remediat: For each partition without the index, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on the partition, then ALTER INDEX <partitioned index> ATTACH PARTITION <new index>. The partitioned index becomes valid once every partition has one attached.
advisor.partition.parent_not_analyzed.ti: Partitioned table {table} has never been analyzed
advisor.partition.parent_not_analyzed.de: {table} in database {datname} holds about {rows} rows in {partitions} partitions, but has no statistics of its own: autovacuum analyzes partitions, never a partitioned table. The planner uses the table's statistics to estimate joins and queries that span partitions.
advisor.partition.parent_not_analyzed.re: ANALYZE {tableSQL}; and again after large changes in its data, for example from a scheduled job.
